title: Philippe Bouvard, radio and television legend, passes away
seoTitle: Philippe Bouvard, Radio and TV Legend, Dies at 96
subtitle: The journalist and host left his mark on generations leading high-ratings programs on radio and television.
excerpt: Host and journalist Philippe Bouvard died at age 96 at his home. He shaped communication history with decades of work at RTL.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Journalist, writer, screenwriter, and host Philippe Bouvard has died at the age of 96 at his residence located in Cannes. His death was announced by his wife, Colette, to the RTL broadcaster, marking the end of a career spanning nearly six decades in the media.

The career at the helm of Les Grosses Têtes

Philippe Bouvard became primarily known for hosting the comedy and entertainment show Les Grosses Têtes on the RTL network. The show premiered in 1977 and regularly gathered over 2.5 million listeners. The host remained at the helm of the format for 37 years, a period that solidified his popularity with the public.

Television success with Le Théâtre de Bouvard

In addition to radio, the host made his mark on television with the program Le Théâtre de Bouvard, aired on Antenne 2 between 1982 and 1986. The show featured short sketches and served as a training ground for comedians, helping launch the careers of various artists who became major names in French comedy.

Retirement and final years of activity

In recent years, the former host considerably reduced his activities and retired from the airwaves. In June 2024, he announced that he would permanently leave radio, celebrating the symbolic milestone of sixty years of presence on RTL. Even after stepping down from the main hosting duties of the radio show, he remained connected to the station through columns and segments.

Tributes and reaction to his death

His passing mobilized public figures, including French President Emmanuel Macron, who paid tribute to the journalist. Macron emphasized that Philippe Bouvard accompanied generations with his voice, freedom of tone, and wit, stating that the country has lost a free spirit.

With information from Sortir à Paris, Metrópoles.
